The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Winding/Number/Basic.lean#L72) implements [Hungerbühler–Wasem Definition2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.00997): excision is by complex-plane distance ‖γ(t)−z₀‖>ε, with ε→0 from above, not by equal parameter intervals. This distinction makes the principal-value convention geometric even for unequal traversal speeds. The factor (2πi)⁻¹ and interval orientation are correct.

The carrier ℂ intentionally permits fractional on-curve values. The definition itself imposes no regularity or limit existence, and its documentation explicitly labels the undefined-limit case as junk. The separate HasCauchyPVAt predicate requires both eventual integrability of the excised integrand and convergence; it cannot certify a principal value merely because nonintegrable Bochner integrals default to zero. On a continuous rectifiable curve avoiding z₀, the proved bridge recovers the ordinary index. Constant curves and zero-length intervals give zero. Merely closing a nontrivial curve does not force zero winding.

The directly relevant [worked checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L218) all have actual source proofs: [inside and outside circle values](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Winding/Number/Circle.lean#L182), [closed model-sector value](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/ModelSector/Closed.lean#L241), its half and sixth-angle specializations, and the concrete half-disc inverse-pole principal value. The full residue and improper-integral checks concern later theorems; the foundational value does not itself assert those conclusions.

It does not claim the paper's arbitrary cycles, accumulation-free infinite singular sets or essential-singularity extension.

I unfolded both regularity hypotheses. ConditionAprime requires finite crossings and perpendicular tangent-line distance of little-o order equal to the actual pole order. It is independent of along-tangent speed. ConditionB requires rational corner angle and an actual local Laurent splitting whose surviving higher-order terms satisfy (pole exponent−1)·angle∈2πℤ. These are geometric/algebraic inputs, not assumptions that the desired principal value already exists. Simple poles impose no extra resonance requirement. Null-homology retains vanishing index outside U; merely avoiding other singularities would not suffice on a domain with holes.

The conclusion HasCauchyPV requires eventually integrable excisions and convergence for one finite excision set, so no zero-integral fallback proves it vacuously. The source constructs the polar part and kills the analytic remainder by the homology Cauchy theorem. All five [worked criteria](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L218) pass in inspected source: model sectors, interior/exterior circles, the two-simple-pole circle identity, the actual inverse-pole half-disc value πi, and the genuine Dirichlet improper integral π/2. These examples also establish nonvacuity of the on-contour hypotheses.

The [theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/HomologyCauchy.lean#L98) is the exact [Layer3 homology form of Cauchy's theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L184). IsNullHomologous means zero generalized index about every point outside Ω. Because the curve lies inside Ω and is piecewise C¹, those exterior points are avoided and the generalized index reduces to the ordinary index; there is no junk-value loophole in this hypothesis. The condition allows a domain with holes provided the particular cycle has zero index around them. It neither assumes global simple connectivity nor confuses null-homology with null-homotopy.

The output is the actual oriented interval integral of γ′·f(γ). Piecewise C¹ regularity supplies an integrable derivative; continuity of f on the compact trace supplies integrability of the product. Thus the zero conclusion is substantive. IsPiecewiseC1On permits corners and stationary pieces without an unnecessary immersion assumption. Reversed endpoints retain orientation, and equal endpoints of the parameter interval give the ordinary zero-length case. Curve membership forces Ω nonempty even when a=b.

Layer3 has no separate concrete acceptance example. The inspected [star-shaped and disc corollaries](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/StarConvex.lean#L115) discharge null-homology and give genuine closed-curve Cauchy theorems, registering useful consistency checks. The later half-residue and improper-integral criteria belong to the generalized residue theorem and have been checked separately. Dixon's auxiliary point is constructed from the open domain and compact curve, not added as a hidden existence premise. No independent reading of Dixon's 1971 article is claimed.

The [argument principle](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Argument/Principle.lean#L246) has the exact signed multiplicity convention of the [Layer2 target](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L177): positive meromorphic orders count zeros and negative orders count poles, with the counterclockwise factor 2πi. S is a finite set containing every nonzero-order point of the closed disc and lying strictly inside it. Consequently boundary orders are zero. The integer-order hypothesis excludes identically-zero germs (order∞), and harmless extra regular points in S contribute zero.

MeromorphicOn is punctured-germ based, so raw values at removable discontinuities need not already be analytic. The theorem handles this genuine Lean edge case: [normal-form transport](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Argument/Principle.lean#L173) proves that replacing f by its meromorphic normal form changes the logarithmic derivative only on a discrete subset of the circle and leaves the integral unchanged. The normalized function is analytic and nonzero near every boundary point. Thus the result does not rely on totalized deriv or division masking a boundary zero. R>0 also excludes a collapsed contour.

The [residue/order identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Residue/LogDeriv.lean#L63) and [one-point local specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Argument/Principle.lean#L295) are proved and registered. The directly related [classical calibration](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L224) passes in circleIntegral_twoPrincipalParts_eq_residue_sum; its zero-second-coefficient specialization gives the one-pole kernel integral. On-contour zeros and poles are deliberately outside this circle theorem and require the separate principal-value version. No stronger canonical choice of S or order function is asserted; the sum ignores zero orders. In particular it uses d, not its inverse, and the subsequent nebentypus bridge has eigenvalue χ(d). It acts on Mathlib's existing modular forms as a complex linear map.

Choice of lift is eliminated by slash_eq_of_Gamma0Map_eq: equal labels differ by Gamma1(N). I inspected this argument, the explicit surjectivity proof of the label map, coe_diamondOp, the identity and composition laws, and cusp-form compatibility. No positivity assumption on N is necessary here: at N=0 the label group is the units of ℤ and diagonal unit lifts still exist; at N=1 the sole operator is the identity. The unit-typed index excludes noncoprime labels, which are zero-extended only in the separately named diamondOpNat.

These proved laws and the nebentypus iff discharge the direct Layer-0 requirements. No separate numerical Check is attached to this operator; the Delta Hecke eigenvalue and Fricke-sign examples concern later operators.
